title: The world's religions in numbers
examples: What is the largest religion in the world?
How many people are not religious?

explain.say: In 2020 there were about eight billion people in the world. Researchers at the Pew Research Center studied thousands of censuses and surveys to estimate how many belong to each religion, or to none.

Here is the result. Christians are the largest group, at 28.8 percent, then Muslims at 25.6 percent, and the religiously unaffiliated at 24.2 percent. Hindus make up 14.9 percent and Buddhists 4.1 percent.

In people, that is about 2.3 billion Christians, 2 billion Muslims, 1.9 billion unaffiliated, 1.2 billion Hindus and about 324 million Buddhists. Jews number about 15 million, a small share but an ancient and influential faith.

faq.q: What is the largest religion in the world?
faq.a: Christianity is the largest religion, with about 2.3 billion followers, or 28.8 percent of the world's people in 2020, according to the Pew Research Center. Islam is second, with about 2 billion, or 25.6 percent.
asks: which religion has the most followers

faq.a: Between 2010 and 2020, Islam was the fastest-growing major religion, according to Pew. That is mainly because Muslims have the youngest average age and the highest birth rates, not mainly because of conversion. The share of religiously unaffiliated people also grew.

faq.q: How many people are not religious?
faq.a: In 2020 about 1.9 billion people, 24.2 percent of the world, were religiously unaffiliated, according to Pew. That makes them the third-largest group after Christians and Muslims. Many live in China, where most people say they have no religion.
asks: how many people have no religion

faq.q: How many Muslims are there in the world?
faq.a: There were about 2 billion Muslims in 2020, 25.6 percent of the world's population, according to Pew. Countries with the largest Muslim populations include Indonesia, Pakistan, India and Bangladesh.

faq.q: How many Christians are there in the world?
faq.a: There were about 2.3 billion Christians in 2020, 28.8 percent of the world, according to Pew. They live on every continent, and by 2020 sub-Saharan Africa had overtaken Europe as the region with the most Christians.
There were about 1.2 billion Hindus in 2020, 14.9 percent of the world, according to Pew. The great majority live in India, with large communities in Nepal, Bangladesh and around the world.

There were about 324 million Buddhists in 2020, about 4.1 percent of the world, according to Pew. The largest Buddhist population is in China, and Buddhists are a majority in countries such as Thailand, Cambodia, Myanmar, Sri Lanka and Bhutan.

faq.q: How many Jews are there in the world?
faq.a: There were about 14.8 million Jews in 2020, about 0.2 percent of the world, according to Pew. Most live in Israel or the United States. Though small in number, Judaism is ancient and deeply influential, as the root of both Christianity and Islam.
asks: how many Jewish people are there
why are there so few Jews

faq.a: There are around 25 to 30 million Sikhs, which makes Sikhism one of the larger world religions though it is a small share of the world. Most live in the Punjab in India, with large communities in Canada, Britain and the United States.
asks: number of Sikhs in the world

faq.a: The religiously unaffiliated, sometimes called the nones, are people who say they are atheists, agnostics, or nothing in particular. They do not belong to a religion, but many still believe in God or a higher power, or take part in some spiritual practices.

faq.q: Why is the number of non-religious people growing?
faq.a: Pew found the share of unaffiliated people grew between 2010 and 2020, mainly because some people raised in a religion, often Christianity, stopped identifying with it, especially in places like Europe, North America and parts of East Asia. Researchers call this religious switching.

Researchers combine national censuses and large surveys that ask people which religion, if any, they belong to. These are careful estimates, because some countries never ask about religion and people may belong to one faith while practising others.
asks: how do we know how many people are religious
where do religion statistics come from

faq.q: Which country has the most Christians?
faq.a: The United States has the largest Christian population of any country, followed by countries such as Brazil and Mexico. Sub-Saharan Africa, as a region, now has more Christians than Europe.

Pew's other religions group, about 2.2 percent of the world, includes Sikhs, Jains, Bahá'ís, Daoists, Shinto followers, Zoroastrians and many folk and Indigenous traditions. Each is small as a share of the world, but some have many millions of followers.

facts: Pew Research 2020: Christians 28.8 percent of the world, about 2.3 billion people.
Pew Research 2020: Muslims 25.6 percent, about 2 billion; religiously unaffiliated 24.2 percent, about 1.9 billion.
Pew Research 2020: Hindus 14.9 percent, about 1.2 billion; Buddhists 4.1 percent, about 324 million.
Pew Research 2020: Jews about 0.2 percent of the world, about 14.8 million people.
Islam was the fastest-growing major religion from 2010 to 2020, mainly because of a young population and higher birth rates.
